t: A league of mainly German merchant towns, led by Lübeck, that dominated Baltic and North Sea trade from the 14th to the 16th century.
It had no constitution, army or treasury; diets coordinated policy, and four great Kontore traded at Novgorod, Bergen, Bruges and London.
Strong territorial states, Dutch competition and the shift of trade to the Atlantic eroded it; the last diet met in 1669.
dyk: In 1473 the Danzig privateer Paul Beneke captured a ship carrying Hans Memling’s Last Judgment triptych; the altarpiece was taken to Danzig and is still in Gdańsk today.
ev: Henry the Lion refounds Lübeck, the future head of the Hansa
The first general Hanseatic diet meets in Lübeck
The Peace of Stralsund ends the war with Valdemar IV of Denmark
The Treaty of Utrecht confirms Hanseatic privileges in England
Ivan III closes the Hanseatic office at Novgorod
Elizabeth I revokes the privileges of the London Steelyard
The last Hanseatic diet meets in Lübeck

f.founder: North German merchant towns led by Lübeck
f.successor: Free cities of Lübeck, Hamburg and Bremen
